decomposition_notes: Sizing-driven split. The requirements doc describes a decision-then-execute initiative whose full task count (measurement + decision + first-vertical-slice) would total 14 tasks, well past the ~10-task soft cap. Split at the natural decide-vs-execute seam: G1 owns measurement + the decision document; G2 owns the first vertical slice of whichever path the decision selects. CROSS-GOAL CLAIM ORDERING: Claim G1 first and let its final task (the decision document) land in main BEFORE claiming G2. G2's first task cannot be scoped without G1's recommendation — its acceptance criteria reference the path G1 selects. Within each goal, tasks use array-index dependencies for sibling sequencing.

goals.title: Measure the current test suite and produce a decision document
goals.why: Today the test-suite question is debated on vibes — no one has data on which tests are slow, how often they flake, or what the mock-to-integration ratio looks like per module. Decisions land badly when nobody has the numbers.
goals.what: Capture baseline measurements, build a pain inventory, evaluate three candidate paths (status-quo-tighten / convention-overhaul / parallel-replacement), recommend one, and define the first vertical slice for whichever path is chosen.
goals.description: Decision artifact, not implementation. The output is a committed Markdown decision document that names the recommended path and the first vertical slice. G2 picks up from there.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
Baseline measurements committed to a fixture
Pain inventory captured with concrete examples
Three candidate paths evaluated against the same rubric
A single recommendation is named with rationale
The first vertical slice is specified well enough that G2 can start without re-derivation
pitfalls: Do not skip the measurement pass — the cap of the whole initiative is that decisions need data, not vibes
Do not predetermine the recommendation before the data is in

tasks.title: Capture slowest-20 tests baseline
tasks.description: Run `mix test --trace --slowest 20` (or the framework equivalent) and commit the output as a baseline fixture. Includes wall-clock per test, file path, and tag.
tasks.why: The slow-suite complaint is anecdotal; a committed slowest-20 baseline turns it into evidence the path evaluations can score against.
tasks.what: Run mix test --trace --slowest 20, capture wall-clock, file path, and tag per test, and commit the output as a fixture.
tasks.where_context: fixtures/test-suite-baseline-slowest-20.txt (new); run from the repo root against test/
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Output committed at fixtures/test-suite-baseline-slowest-20.txt
Re-running on the same suite produces equivalent results (within 5%)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Run on a quiet machine with the seed pinned, twice — commit the second run
Record Elixir/OTP versions and total suite time in a header comment
pitfalls: Timings vary with machine load — the 5% reproducibility criterion fails on a busy laptop
Do not fix any slow test you spot; measurement only

unit_tests: Not applicable — measurement task, no production code
manual_tests: Re-run the command and confirm the top-20 set matches within the 5% tolerance
edge_cases: Setup-heavy tests may swap ranks between runs — note ties in the fixture header

security_considerations: None — committed fixture contains test names and timings only

tasks.title: Capture mock-to-integration ratio per module
tasks.description: Walk test/ directory; per module, count tests using Mox/stubs vs tests using Repo.checkout/Bypass. Commit the table as a baseline fixture.
tasks.why: The mock-vs-integration debate is the heart of the disagreement; a per-module ratio shows where the suite actually stands.
tasks.what: Walk test/, count Mox/stub-based vs Repo.checkout/Bypass-based tests per top-level module, and commit the table.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Table committed at fixtures/test-suite-baseline-mock-ratio.md
Includes one row per top-level module in test/
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Classify via grep heuristics (import Mox / verify_on_exit vs DataCase / Bypass.open)
State the classification rule in the doc so the table can be re-derived
pitfalls: Files mixing both styles count in both columns — do not guess them into one
Do not editorialize in the table; the path evals interpret, this task measures

verification_steps.step_text: Spot-check 3 modules in the table against actual test files

manual_tests: Spot-check 3 modules against actual test files per the verification step
edge_cases: Shared helpers and zero-assertion files — exclude them and note the exclusion rule

security_considerations: None — analysis of test files; the output is a counts table

tasks.title: Capture flake rate over the last 14 CI days
tasks.description: Scrape recent CI runs (or a representative log archive) and tally tests that flipped pass/fail without code changes. Commit per-test flake count.
tasks.why: Flakes are the most rage-inducing failure mode; without a 14-day tally nobody knows if it is three bad tests or thirty.
tasks.what: Scrape the last 14 days of CI runs, tally tests that flipped pass/fail with no code change, and commit per-test counts plus the aggregate rate.
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Define 'flake' precisely (same commit SHA, differing outcomes) and state it in the CSV header
Keep CI run IDs per row so counts are auditable
pitfalls: Retried-and-passed runs hide flakes — count the retry, not just the final status
The 14-day window may straddle a CI config change; note any discontinuity

verification_steps.step_text: Cross-reference CSV against a sample CI log

manual_tests: Cross-reference the CSV against a sample CI log per the verification step
edge_cases: Tests renamed mid-window — match by file and line, or record as unmatched

security_considerations: Scrub CI log excerpts before committing — raw CI logs can contain env vars, tokens, or internal URLs
CI API credentials used for scraping stay in the environment, never in the fixture or committed scripts

tasks.title: Build the pain inventory with concrete examples
tasks.description: Walk through 5-10 specific moments where the current architecture slowed a contributor down — with file paths, PR links, or commit refs as evidence.
tasks.why: Numbers say what is slow; the inventory says why anyone cares — it keeps the decision anchored to real contributor moments.
tasks.what: Document 5-10 concrete moments the current test architecture slowed a contributor down, each with a PR link, commit ref, or file path.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-pain-inventory.md committed
Each item has at least one concrete reference (PR / commit / file)
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
One item per pain, each with an evidence link plus a one-paragraph narrative
Tag each item with the candidate path (A/B/C) it most bears on
pitfalls: Vibes disguised as items — every entry needs a concrete reference per the acceptance criteria
Do not rank or recommend here; that is the recommendation task's job

verification_steps.step_text: Review committed file for concrete references

manual_tests: Review the committed file and confirm every item carries at least one concrete reference
edge_cases: Pains with no linkable evidence get dropped or explicitly marked anecdotal

security_considerations: None — internal documentation; references are to internal PRs and commits

tasks.title: Evaluate path A: status quo + tighten slow tests
tasks.description: Score Path A against the measurement data. Estimate effort to bring the slowest-20 tests under target.
tasks.why: Status-quo-tighten is the cheapest path; scoring it honestly against the data guards against shiny-rewrite bias.
tasks.what: Score Path A against the slowest-20, mock-ratio, and flake baselines; estimate the effort to bring the slowest-20 under target.
tasks.where_context: docs/decisions/test-suite-path-a.md (new); inputs are the three baseline fixtures and the pain inventory
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use the same rubric headings as the B and C evals so the recommendation can compare side by side
Cite fixture rows, not impressions
pitfalls: Effort estimates without opening the actual slow tests are vibes — read the top offenders
Do not let A become a strawman just because it is unexciting

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review the eval against the data fixtures per the verification step — every claim traces to a fixture row
edge_cases: Metrics that cut in opposite directions (fast but flaky) — the rubric must score them separately

tasks.title: Evaluate path B: convention overhaul without replacement
tasks.description: Score Path B (mandate Bypass for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB, kill mox stubs) against the measurement data.
tasks.why: Convention overhaul promises the benefits of replacement without migration cost; the data says whether the current suite can actually converge.
tasks.what: Score Path B (mandate Bypass for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB, retire Mox stubs) against the same rubric and baselines as A and C.
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Same rubric headings as the A and C evals
Use the mock-ratio fixture to size how much of the suite the mandate would touch
pitfalls: A convention nobody enforces is Path A with extra steps — the eval must address enforcement (Credo rule or CI check)

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review the eval against the data fixtures per the verification step
edge_cases: Modules where the mandate is impractical (third-party SDK seams) — the eval must name the exceptions policy

tasks.title: Evaluate path C: parallel replacement under test_v2
tasks.description: Score Path C (start a parallel test architecture; migrate module by module) against the measurement data.
tasks.why: Parallel replacement is the highest-cost, highest-upside option; it needs the most sober scoring because rewrites always look cleaner than they land.
tasks.what: Score Path C (parallel test_v2/ architecture, migrated module by module) against the shared rubric and baselines.
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Same rubric headings as the A and B evals
Address the two-suites transition cost explicitly: CI time, contributor confusion, drift risk
pitfalls: The eval must name an end state and an abandonment criterion — parallel suites that never converge are the known failure mode

verification_steps.step_text: Review eval against the data fixtures

manual_tests: Review the eval against the data fixtures per the verification step
edge_cases: Doubled CI wall-clock during the transition — the eval must quantify it from the baseline

tasks.title: Write the recommendation and first-vertical-slice spec
tasks.description: Pick one of A/B/C with rationale; name the first vertical slice (specific module to migrate / specific tests to tighten / specific convention to mandate) that G2 will execute.
tasks.why: This document is the entire point of G1 — one named path with rationale, specific enough that G2 starts without re-litigating.
tasks.what: Pick A, B, or C with data-grounded rationale and specify the first vertical slice (module, tests, or convention) that G2 will execute.
tasks.where_context: docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md (new); inputs are the three path evals and the pain inventory
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md committed
First vertical slice is specific enough that G2 can scope tasks without re-derivation
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
State the decision first, rationale second, first slice third
The first-slice spec names exact files/modules and the target metric delta
pitfalls: A hedged recommendation ('mostly B with some C') recreates the ambiguity this goal exists to kill
A first slice scoped too big — it should be one G2-sized bite

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm the recommendation names the first vertical slice precisely

manual_tests: Confirm the first vertical slice is unambiguous per the verification step — a reader can name the files G2 will touch
edge_cases: Evals producing a near-tie — the doc must state the tiebreaker used

goals.title: Implement the first vertical slice from the test-suite decision
goals.why: The decision document from G1 names a specific first vertical slice. G2 ships it.
goals.what: Execute the first vertical slice as specified in docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md. The exact scope depends on the recommendation: tightening the slowest-20 (Path A), enforcing a convention on a representative module (Path B), or migrating one module under test_v2/ (Path C).
goals.where_context: test/ — exact paths depend on the recommendation
goals.description: BLOCKED on G1. The first task here cannot be scoped until docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md lands in main with the first-vertical-slice spec.
goals.acceptance_criteria:
First vertical slice as specified is implemented
Before/after measurements show the expected delta (faster, fewer mocks, etc.)
No regression in pass rate of the existing suite
Documentation updated to reflect the new convention or layer
pitfalls: Do not deviate from the recommendation's first-slice scope — broader changes belong in follow-up tasks
Do not break the existing `mix test` and `mix test --cover` entry points

tasks.title: Re-read the recommendation and confirm the first-vertical-slice scope
tasks.description: Open docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md, identify the named first slice, and confirm the scope is still applicable (no relevant test changes since G1 landed).
tasks.why: Time may have passed since G1 landed; confirming the slice is still applicable prevents executing a stale plan.
tasks.what: Read docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md, verify the named slice against current test/ contents, and note confirmation or flag a refresh.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Notes added to the recommendation doc confirming the slice scope or flagging the need for a recommendation refresh
tasks.patterns_to_follow: Append a dated confirmation note to the doc rather than editing the original recommendation text
pitfalls: If the slice's target tests changed since G1 landed, flag for a refresh — do not silently re-scope

verification_steps.step_text: Read the slice description against current test/ contents

manual_tests: Read the slice description against current test/ contents per the verification step
edge_cases: Recommendation references files that were moved or renamed since G1

tasks.title: Implement the first slice — primary code change
tasks.description: Make the changes called for by the first vertical slice. Exact files depend on the recommendation; the test description there is your scope.
tasks.why: This is the initiative's first real payoff — proof the chosen path produces the predicted improvement on real code.
tasks.what: Make the code changes the first vertical slice calls for; exact files come from the recommendation (tighten slowest tests, enforce a convention on one module, or migrate one module under test_v2/).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
Code change as specified is in place
Unit tests pass after the change
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Follow the conventions the recommendation mandates (e.g., Bypass over Mox for HTTP, Repo.checkout for DB) exactly as written
Keep the diff within the named slice
pitfalls: Scope creep into neighboring modules — broader changes belong in follow-up slices
Do not delete failing tests to hit the metric; convert or fix them

unit_tests: The affected module's tests pass under the new pattern
integration_tests: Full mix test run stays green
manual_tests: Not applicable — the suite itself is the verification
edge_cases: Async-unsafe tests exposed by conversion (shared state, sandbox ownership)
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Coverage of the touched module at or above its pre-slice figure

security_considerations: Test fixtures introduced by the slice use fake credentials and tokens only — never copy real secrets or production data into test/ or fixtures/
Any Bypass/HTTP stub servers must bind to localhost only

tasks.title: Capture before/after measurement against the slice's target metric
tasks.description: Run the same measurement procedure G1 ran for the affected module; commit the after-figure.
tasks.why: The slice was chosen to move a specific metric; without the after-measurement the initiative cannot prove the path works.
tasks.what: Re-run G1's measurement procedure for the affected module and commit a before/after table.
tasks.where_context: fixtures/test-suite-slice-after.md (new); before-figures come from the G1 baseline fixtures
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Use the identical command and environment as the G1 baseline capture
Present before, after, delta, and the recommendation's predicted delta side by side
pitfalls: Measuring on different hardware than the baseline invalidates the comparison — note the environment in both fixtures

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm before/after delta matches the recommendation's predicted delta

manual_tests: Confirm the delta matches or beats the recommendation's prediction per the verification step
edge_cases: Delta lands under prediction — record it honestly; the follow-up-slices task consumes this signal
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Not applicable — no production code changed

security_considerations: None — measurement task; output is a timings/counts table

tasks.title: Confirm no regression in pass rate on the existing suite
tasks.description: Run `mix test --cover` end-to-end; verify pass rate and coverage match baseline.
tasks.why: A slice that speeds one module while breaking the suite's entry points is a net loss; this is the safety gate before docs and follow-ups.
tasks.what: Run mix test --cover end to end and verify pass rate and coverage are at or above baseline.
tasks.where_context: Repo root; compared against the G1 baseline fixtures
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
mix test --cover passes
Coverage unchanged or improved relative to baseline
tasks.patterns_to_follow: Run the exact entry points the goal pitfalls protect: mix test and mix test --cover
pitfalls: Coverage can drop legitimately if the slice deleted redundant tests — explain any delta rather than gaming it

verification_steps.expected_result: All tests pass; coverage at/above baseline

unit_tests: Not applicable — this task is itself the suite run
manual_tests: Compare the coverage summary against the baseline figure
edge_cases: Known flaky tests (from the G1 flake CSV) failing unrelated to the slice — rerun and attribute correctly
testing_strategy.coverage_target: Suite coverage at or above the pre-slice baseline

security_considerations: None — verification run, no code changed

tasks.title: Update CONTRIBUTING / AGENTS notes to reflect the new convention
tasks.description: Adjust the project's contributor docs so the next contributor knows about the new pattern or layering established by the slice.
tasks.why: A convention that lives only in the slice author's head decays instantly; contributor docs are how the pattern survives the next PR.
tasks.what: Update AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md to name the new convention or layer the slice established, with a pointer to an exemplar test file.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md updated
The new convention is named explicitly
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Name the convention explicitly and link the exemplar file from the slice
Match the existing tone and section structure of the doc
pitfalls: Do not document aspiration — only what the slice actually established

manual_tests: Re-read the updated section per the verification step; a new contributor can find the exemplar file from it
edge_cases: Doc guidance conflicting with an older section — reconcile rather than append a contradiction

tasks.title: Define follow-up slices and update the recommendation doc
tasks.description: Based on what worked and what surprised in the first slice, define the next 2-3 vertical slices in the recommendation doc.
tasks.why: Momentum dies between slices; capturing the next 2-3 while the learning is fresh keeps the migration from stalling at one module.
tasks.what: Add a 'Follow-up slices' section to the recommendation doc defining the next 2-3 slices, informed by what the first slice confirmed or surprised on.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
docs/decisions/test-suite-recommendation.md gets a 'Follow-up slices' section
Each next-slice item is specific enough to become a Stride task
tasks.patterns_to_follow:
Same specificity bar as the first slice: named modules, target metric, predicted delta
Each item sized to become one Stride task
pitfalls: Vague follow-ups ('migrate more modules') fail the acceptance criteria — each must be scopable without further discussion

verification_steps.step_text: Confirm each next slice can be scoped without further discussion

manual_tests: Confirm each next slice can be scoped without further discussion per the verification step
edge_cases: First-slice measurement undershot prediction — follow-ups must address the gap, not ignore it
